{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My brother-in-law is the most selfish person I know—never helps with dishes, always takes the last slice, complains about every family obligation. When my daughter was diagnosed with leukemia, he quit his job to drive her to every chemo appointment. Spent his savings on her treatments without being asked. I never knew who he really was until it mattered.

CANDIDATE A:
My quiet, timid coworker never spoke up in meetings, never challenged anyone. When our manager started taking credit for our team's work, she walked into the VP's office with documentation of every stolen idea. Got our manager fired. I'd mistaken her silence for weakness.

CANDIDATE B:
My brother-in-law is the most selfish person I know. When my wife was diagnosed with leukemia, he sent a card and visited once. He complained about the hospital parking and left after an hour. The crisis confirmed exactly who he was—no hidden depths, no surprise transformation.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:17"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories reveal a surprising depth of character in someone initially perceived as weak or selfish during a crisis, leading to a reevaluation of their true nature."}
